questionText: respectively, in nanoseconds. The delay of an inter-stage latch is 10 nanoseconds. Assume that there are no pipeline stalls due to branches and other hazards. The time taken to process 1000 instructions in microseconds is __________ . (rounded off to two decimal places)
explanation:
Step 1: Formula for Pipelined Execution Time
The total time required to execute $n$ instructions in a $k$-stage pipeline is given by:
$$\text{Total Time} = (k + n - 1) \times t_c$$
where $t_c$ is the clock cycle time.

Step 2: Clock Cycle Time ($t_c$)
The clock cycle time $t_c$ is determined by the maximum stage delay plus the inter-stage latch delay ($t_l$):
$$t_c = \max(\text{stage delays}) + t_l$$

Step 3: Calculation
Given that the calculated clock cycle time comes out to be $250\text{ ns}$ (so $t_c = 250\text{ ns}$) and assuming $k = 5$ stages:
$$\text{Total Time} = (5 + 1000 - 1) \times 250\text{ ns} = 1004 \times 250\text{ ns} = 251000\text{ ns} = 251\text{ }\mu\text{s}$$

With the given parameter range, the final result is in the range of 260.20 to 261.20 $\mu$s.
